stories.headline: Lab-raised sunflower sea stars hunted urchins in the wild
stories.summary: In a test release, a dozen-plus lab-raised stars quickly ate sea urchins in Monterey Bay. A disease killed about 6 billion of them, and since then urchins have chewed through kelp forests.
stories.why: If the stars return for good, they could help kelp forests grow back.

stories.stat_label: years the light traveled to us
stories.headline: Telescopes caught gamma rays from a blazar 8 billion light-years away
stories.summary: The LST-1 and MAGIC telescopes picked up high-energy gamma rays from blazar OP 313, a black hole firing a jet straight at Earth. We see it as it was 5 billion years after the Big Bang.
stories.why: It shows how giant black holes accelerated particles in the young universe.

stories.stat_label: for 1,600 m, barefoot in a saree
stories.headline: A 39-year-old mum ran 1,600 m barefoot in a saree
stories.summary: Kavita, a widowed daily-wage worker with 2 kids, trains each morning for a Home Guard job. In a trial run she finished 1,600 metres in 6 minutes 45 seconds, barefoot and in a saree.
stories.why: She's chasing a steady job so her children can keep studying.

stories.headline: A teacher treks 5 km through leopard forest to teach 2 girls
stories.summary: For 13 years Jeevan Mithari has walked a steep forest trail with gaurs, wild dogs and leopards to a hamlet school. Today it has 2 students: sisters aged 8 and 5. The older one wants to be a doctor.
stories.why: Without him, the nearest school is 8 km away and the girls would drop out.

fun_fact: Sunflower sea stars can have up to 24 arms.
